title: Antigravity Vs Replit (24 hours in)
author: Shnatrix
selftext:
Hi guys,

  
I'm a vibe coding complete noob. I love vibe coding and love being able to create exact tools for work, play and even a game I'm casually building.

What I don't love is spending money, like most people vibe coding out things they've always dreamed of doing, we are doing it now because we can and it's affordable. Rather than paying a coder for a niche tool or game or side project that could cost $1,000s if not $10,000s + 

  
However Replit for this month... yes month... so far... yes it hasn't ended yet - I'm already at $550usd in computing time.

  
Enough to make my cry. SOOO What do I do - I go to Antigravity to see if I can get similarly impressive things for free.

  
Well I guess you can - however it's no where near the same thing. 

I find with replit - I have a problem it finds the solution.  
I find with Antigravity - I have a problem, it wants to build a solution - and building solutions costs time.

  
So what have I found out? Time = money and I am coming to the realisation I am okay with spending that money to get a faster and easier service.

  
So to me no Replit isn't dead - but I would love a more cost effective way to game dev.

  
Anyone cooking with anything good atm?

comments.author: kaayotee
comments.body: As long as you can move your code to your own git repo, just commit everything out from replit and start using claude code. It's $20 monthly subscription and if you want high usage get the max $100 plan

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body:
There is no limit? I have also looked at Claude - but not really delved too deep into it, because I was committed on replit

Are you building in Claude?

replies.author: kaayotee
replies.body:
There is daily and weekly limit. I have been using claude web from 1.5 yrs and claude code since it launched. Vibe coded 3 SaaS all the way to production, the daily/ weekly limit are good enough to make complicated projects. I am software engineer by profession so know a bit better on how to keep the token usage under check by iteratively working on features rather then everything in one go.

2 of my SaaS that are running out their, built completely using claude code all by spending $20 a month 

https://subscene.io

https://battleborg.ai ( Game, not SaaS)

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body: Very impressive - I'll look at this as a pivot. Thank you

replies.author: brianlmerritt
replies.body: The secret of Claude Code and similar with limits is to limit your debugs.  You can burn through a weeks usage by saying repeatedly "No, this still isn't working".  I find it easier to just change models on free or low cost tiers, e.g. if Claude doesn't get it give both Gemini 3 and GPT-5.1 a go to see which gets there first.

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body:
Helpful - but how do you push the issue into GPT or Gem3 ?

Example I'm having issues currently with some hardening and anti-cheat.  
So how would they be able to pick it up?

Or you connect in git and push to each for a check?

replies.author: brianlmerritt
replies.body:
Mostly I develop in vscode and have the low cost github option, plus claude code plugin there.  So that gives me most models at once - just have to ensure relevant files are included in the new chats.  I use claude code for most development, then hop back out to github copilot as needed.

Also now using antigravity because I work for a university and Google gave me free 14 months or so of Google pro.  TBH I haven't done enough development in that to see what limits there are, if any.

comments.author: Own-Detective-A
comments.body:
Oof, 550 usd a month to prototype a game?


Why not learn programing at this rate?

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body: I have a particular set of skills.... Coding and patience ain't one of them lol

replies.author: Bluetails_Buizel
replies.body: You mean you prefer to spend more time on art or programming isn’t your thing? Too difficult to learn?

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body: I am neither artistic or a programmer, I am in sales by trade. Conversation is my skill set. So it doesn't translate here - But I enjoy the art and process of building things.

replies.author: mrpoopybruh
replies.body: I mean, as a programmer, who is making a game, I'm considering vibe coding up most of it (esp the web portions and support site), because 550 is much cheaper than my time fwiw

comments.author: Shnatrix
comments.body: 1 month in - I reverse my decision lol - I now built in antigravity - push to replit via github. Good times.
